fact: UNESCO's project 3210652071 (USD 166,800, 66% progress, 2024-2025) on digital skills and media and information literacy for populations is on going, with an allocation to this country (Gabon 10%).

Under the 2 March 2026 MoU with Smart Africa, the Smart Africa Digital Academy is to be deployed in Gabon with training for young people, professionals and entrepreneurs, coordinated by the Ministry of Digital Economy.

Gabonmediatime reports the Ministry of Digital Economy, with UNESCO and two universities, launched the Global Skills Academy on 15 October 2024, offering 2,000 free certified digital courses to Gabonese learners, young women, vulnerable people and civil servants; no number trained is given.
ANINF and Cybastion launched the free Africa DigiEmpower digital and cybersecurity training programme for 1,000 young Gabonese on 27 January 2026, with three levels hosted at the ANINF Academy.

Gabonactu reports the Digital Economy ministry, with Smart Africa, SPIN and the Centre gabonais de l'innovation, officially launched the Smart Africa Youth Chapter Gabon on 2 May 2026, an online five-module programme with more than 2,000 young people already enrolled in phase one.

fact: The national digital infrastructure agency ANINF, with Cybastion, launched the first free certified digital-skills and cybersecurity cohort of 150 young Gabonese in Libreville on 13 April 2026, within a commitment to train 1,000 under DigiEmpower.

We Are Tech says ST DIGITAL inaugurated the CFEP-MTIC vocational training centre in Nkok, teaching web development, mobile applications and IT support, as part of the World Bank-supported PRODECE project.
